message.content:
You're working in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-wip-mailboxes-redesign (branch feature/mailboxes-redesign, already created off latest main, node_modules and .env symlinked from /opt/nxeon). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon directly, do NOT merge or deploy — just make the changes, verify, and report back. Do NOT run `git add -A` (a documented past incident replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink) — stage specific files by name only if you commit (only commit if explicitly asked; leave it uncommitted otherwise and report the diff).

## The problem

The owner of Nxeon (a hosting platform) looked at the live "Mailboxes" / Business Email dashboard page (nxeon.cloud/dashboard/email) and said: "we need to reorganize this mailboxes page, especially when there are a lot of mailboxes, its way too cluttered."

I have screenshots of the live page. It renders one large card per email subscription/domain (e.g. "kodely.me", "testin2g.com", "testing.com", "testing.sites.nxeon.cloud", "kaymo.revsports.ca" — a real test account has 9 subscriptions), and EVERY card is fully expanded at all times, showing: domain name + status badges, plan/usage line, a DNS-verification banner (when unverified), a "Deliverability check" row with a button, a "Mailboxes" section listing every mailbox row (each with Open inbox / Show password / Reset password / Remove buttons), AND a full "NEW MAILBOX" add-form. With 9 subscriptions this becomes an extremely long, repetitive, hard-to-scan page — a wall of near-identical large cards, most of which (per the screenshots) don't even have mailboxes set up yet ("No mailboxes yet — add your first below"). There's no collapsing, no summary view, no way to jump to a specific domain, and setup-incomplete subscriptions get the exact same visual weight as fully active ones with real mailboxes.

## Source of truth

The whole page is rendered by ONE component: components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx (1156 lines), rendered from app/dashboard/email/page.tsx (server component that fetches the data and passes it in — read this too to understand what real data is already available: subscriptions, their plan info, mailbox lists, DNS verification status, deliverability-check state, etc.). app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx also imports `PlanOpt`/`SubscriptionRow` types from EmailHosting.tsx — check whether your changes affect those exported types and keep that import working.

Read EmailHosting.tsx and app/dashboard/email/page.tsx in full before making any changes. Understand:
- The real data shape for a subscription (domain, plan, status, DNS/verification state, deliverability-check state, mailbox array, quota/mailbox-limit).
- Which actions are server actions vs client state (add mailbox, remove mailbox, reset password, show password, check deliverability, verify DNS) so you don't break any real functionality.
- Whether "Show password" reveals a real one-time secret (common for mailbox passwords) — if so, be careful not to break that flow when restructuring.

## What "reorganized, less cluttered" should mean here — use your judgment, but consider:

- **Collapse by default, expand on demand**: each domain/subscription should probably render as a compact summary row/header (domain, status badges, mailbox count, plan) that expands to reveal the full mailbox list + add-form + DNS/deliverability details, rather than every subscription being fully expanded all the time. Consider auto-expanding ones that need attention (e.g. "Setup required"/unverified) and collapsing healthy fully-set-up ones, or make it purely user-toggled — your call, but justify it.
- **Search/filter**: with many subscriptions, a search-by-domain box (this codebase already uses this pattern elsewhere — check components/customer/HostingClient.tsx or similar dashboard list pages for the established search/tab/filter conventions used across the portal, so this page matches the rest of the app rather than inventing a new pattern) would help.
- **De-emphasize incomplete/empty ones**: subscriptions with zero mailboxes and "Setup required" could be visually grouped or pushed down/collapsed rather than taking the same full-height slot as an active one with real mailboxes — but don't hide required actions (DNS setup) from the user; just don't force everyone to scroll past them by default.
- **Reduce per-mailbox-row chrome**: 4 buttons (Open inbox / Show password / Reset password / Remove) per mailbox row, times every mailbox, times every domain, is a lot of visual weight — consider a 3-dot action menu (this codebase's established convention elsewhere, e.g. admin/dashboard list pages) for the less-common actions (Reset password / Remove / Show password) while keeping "Open inbox" as the primary visible action, or similar — your call.
- Keep the top summary card, "How Business Email works" explainer, and the new-subscription wizard steps at the top as-is unless they're clearly part of the clutter problem — the core complaint is specifically about the repeated per-domain cards below "Your email subscriptions."

Look at how other list-heavy dashboard pages in this codebase (e.g. components/customer/HostingClient.tsx if it exists, or the servers/game-servers list pages) already solve "many items, need to stay scannable" — reuse established UI conventions (tabs, search bars, status pills, 3-dot menus, collapsible rows) rather than inventing new ones, so this page feels consistent with the rest of the portal.

## Constraints

- Do not change any real behavior/data flow (server actions, mailbox CRUD, DNS verification, deliverability checks) — this is a presentation/layout reorganization, not a feature change.
- Do not fabricate data or remove real functionality to simplify the UI — every action currently available (Open inbox, Show password, Reset password, Remove, Add mailbox, Check deliverability, Show/Verify DNS records) must remain reachable, just better organized.
- Preserve accessibility basics (keyboard-operable expand/collapse, buttons still real buttons).
- This worktree's .env points at the LIVE production database — do not run anything that writes to it. For visual verification, either build fabricated mock data for a temporary preview route (delete it before finishing, this is the established pattern other agents in this session have used) or carefully use read-only dev-server rendering. Do NOT run broad process-killing commands like `pkill -f "next dev"` — a previous agent this session did that and it matched the live production systemd service's process name pattern too (no harm resulted that time, but scope any process-stopping command by exact PID or port, never a broad pattern match).

## Test baseline

Before your changes, `npm test` in this repo has exactly 34 pre-existing, unrelated failures (pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests) — this is a known, established baseline, not something you introduced. Confirm your change doesn't add any NEW failures beyond that same set of 34.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — must be clean.
2. `npm test` — compare against the 34-failure baseline, confirm zero new failures.
3. Real visual verification: run `next dev` on an isolated port, use a temporary preview route with fabricated data covering the actual clutter scenario (e.g. 9+ subscriptions, a mix of fully-active-with-many-mailboxes, empty/setup-required, and unverified-DNS ones) and screenshot it (desktop + mobile) via Playwright or similar to confirm the reorganization actually reads as less cluttered and everything still works (expand/collapse, search if added, action menus). Delete the temporary preview route afterward.

## Report back

Summarize: what you changed and why, any judgment calls you made (especially around auto-expand/collapse defaults and which actions moved into a menu), confirmation of the 3 verification steps above, and leave the change uncommitted in the worktree for review (per this session's standing rule: only commit when explicitly asked).

## Summary

**File changed:** `/opt/nxeon-wip-mailboxes-redesign/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx` (only this file — `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx` and the exported `PlanOpt`/`SubscriptionRow` types used by `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` are untouched)

**What changed** (presentation only — no server action, data-fetch, or CRUD logic touched):

1. **Collapse by default, expand on demand.** Each subscription now renders as a compact one-line header (domain, status badges, mailbox count, plan) that expands via a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` to reveal the DNS panel, deliverability check, mailbox list, and add-mailbox form — the same content as before, just not force-rendered for every card at once.

2. **Sensible auto-expand/collapse default (judgment call):** a subscription auto-expands if it needs action — `external && !verified` (DNS setup required) or any mailbox with status `FAILED` — otherwise it starts collapsed. Accounts with ≤2 subscriptions always start fully expanded, since there's no clutter to solve there.

3. **Sort by urgency (judgment call):** subscriptions needing attention sort first, then active ones (have mailboxes), then empty "not set up yet" ones sort last — using a stable sort so items within the same group keep their original order. This directly addresses "setup-incomplete subscriptions get the same visual weight as active ones."

4. **Search + filter, matching this codebase's established convention** (`components/customer/ServersList.tsx`'s pill-chip filter pattern, reused verbatim rather than inventing a new one): "All / Needs attention / Active / Not set up yet" chips with live counts, plus a domain search box. Only shown once there are more than 3 subscriptions — a small account doesn't need the extra chrome.

5. **3-dot action menu for mailbox rows (judgment call):** "Open inbox" (and "Retry setup" when applicable) stay as the one/two visible primary action(s); "Show password"/"Refresh password", "Reset password", and "Remove" moved into a new `RowMenu` dropdown, styled and behaviorally identical to the existing `CurrencySwitcher.tsx` dropdown convention (outside-click + Escape to close, `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"`, `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`). All four actions remain one click away; the visible per-row button count just dropped from 4 to 1–2.
